title: Maximum Element-Sum of a Complete Subset of Indices
summary: Given a 1-indexed array nums, choose a complete subset where the product of any two indices is a perfect square.
statement: Given a 1-indexed array nums, choose a complete subset where the product of any two indices is a perfect square. Return the sum of the subset with the highest sum.
constraints: A nonempty subset of one-indexed positions is complete when every pairwise index product is a perfect square.
Return the maximum sum of nums values over complete subsets.
hints: Two indices have square product exactly when their square-free kernels match.
Reduce every one-based index by removing all square factors and group nums by the remainder.
Accumulate each group and return its largest sum.
Equal kernels cancel every odd prime exponent in the product; unequal kernels leave at least one odd exponent.
editorial: Equal kernels cancel every odd prime exponent in the product; unequal kernels leave at least one odd exponent.

tests.explanation: Indices sharing the same square-free kernel form candidate groups; the best group sums to sixteen.
Grouping positions by square-free kernel gives the maximum valid element sum.
